tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final answer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After solving the puzzle, present the complete sequence of moves as a single list in the exact required format.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you have generated the full sequence of legal moves that transforms the initial state to the goal state.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing only a partial list of moves or omitting the list entirely, resulting in an empty or incomplete answer.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free blocked larger disks by moving top smaller disks first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk is not the topmost disk on its peg, first move any smaller disks that sit above it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a larger disk that has smaller disks on top of it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 4 while disk 1 is still on top of it, causing an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate source peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the disk you intend to move is the topmost disk on its source peg; moving any other disk is illegal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before issuing any move, check that the source peg's top disk matches the disk you plan to move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 from a peg where disk 2 is on top, violating the top‑disk rule.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate destination peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a disk, check that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before each move, verify that placing the disk will not put a larger disk on a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 3 onto a peg whose top disk is 2, creating an illegal larger‑on‑smaller situation.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Apply classic Hanoi recursion to generate move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When moving a stack of k disks from one peg to another using the third peg as auxiliary, recursively move k‑1 disks, move the largest, then move the k‑1 disks onto it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you have a clean subproblem of moving a contiguous stack of disks between two pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move a stack of three disks directly without using the recursive pattern, leading to an incomplete or illegal sequence.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear destination peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg currently holds smaller disks that must end up above the larger disk in the final configuration, first move those smaller disks elsewhere.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before moving a larger disk onto a peg that already contains smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 onto a peg where disk 3 is on top, blocking the correct final ordering.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Form classic start by moving smallest disk onto full stack
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When the puzzle starts with all disks on one peg and the goal is to move them to another peg, begin by moving the smallest disk onto the full stack to create a classic start configuration.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: In classic start scenarios where all disks begin on a single peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Leaving the smallest disk on its original peg and attempting to move larger disks directly, causing illegal moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Goal‑first descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When the goal is to stack all disks on a single peg, always move the largest remaining disk that is not yet on the goal peg first.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When assembling the final stack, start by placing the largest missing disk onto the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to place a smaller disk onto the goal peg before the largest missing disk, resulting in later ordering conflicts.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate final configuration after move generation
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the move list, simulate the moves from the initial state to verify that the final configuration matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have generated the full move list, before outputting it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Outputting a move list that leaves a disk on the wrong peg, causing the final state to differ from the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use the smallest disk as a flexible temporary placeholder
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Treat the smallest disk (disk 1) as a universal temporary buffer: move it onto any larger disk or empty peg to free larger disks or clear pegs, and move it again as needed.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a larger disk is blocked by a smaller one, or a peg must be cleared temporarily, move the smallest disk first.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Leaving disk 1 on top of a larger disk that later needs to be placed below that larger disk, causing ordering violations.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may think no moves are needed or may truncate before generating moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always generate at least one legal move when the initial configuration differs from the goal, and ensure the move list is fully output.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Truncated move list (incomplete solution) due to token limit
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of tokens or stops generation prematurely.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Keep reasoning concise, place the full move list at the end, and avoid extra text after it.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (source peg top mismatch)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model forgets to check the source peg's top before moving.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate that the chosen disk is the top disk on its source peg before issuing the move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal placement)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model neglects to verify the destination peg's top disk size.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
